institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have been to France and Paris many times, and I love the culture. So when I had to choose a city to go on exchange to, Paris was an obvious choice, since I have long wanted to improve my French language skills. Additionally, I knew that Sciences Po had a reputation for being very ambitious and academically challenging, which I thought could be interesting to experience myself.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were both positive and less favorable aspects of my exchange stay. Some of the courses I took were incredibly exciting and enriching, while others were downright dull and almost a repetition of courses I had in the first semester of political science in Copenhagen. Experiencing a different teaching culture and a high workload was interesting, but at times, it was also overwhelming and affected my mental well-being. I loved walking around and experiencing Paris with my friends – that was purely enjoyable!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I remember Sciences Po sending a lot of emails containing the necessary information. I do not recall feeling that any information was missing.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: No assistance other than information sent over email. But in my individual case, it was not necessary either.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I have no additional comments.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I did not have the energy to try to navigate the rental market in Paris, so I applied for a spot in the Cité Universitaire. I got a place in the Danish house but was transferred to the Portuguese house through their exchange program. I cannot recommended that specific house.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: My experience is that one either has to be very lucky or willing to spend a lot of money if they do not want to live in a dormitory.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not investigate the housing options offered by Sciences Po. That might have been a mistake on my part.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was not too difficult to understand because it was explained in a webinar, and there was also a very detailed guide document. However, the system itself was not structured very logically, and it was stressful that the courses filled up within a few minutes.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It has been a while, so I do not remember the registration process very clearly. But I recall something about going into the portal and finding the specific courses you wanted to enroll in from the overall list of courses, then clicking on them, and finally saving them all to your user account.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Fortunately, I got all the courses I wanted in the first round, so I did not look into what kind of help was available if something went wrong.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. I got all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read the guide document thoroughly and make sure you understand the registration process. Sit down well in advance with your computer ready. Ensure you have a good internet connection. Keep a cool head.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had both a few really good courses and a few courses I was less pleased with – but I think that is quite common. Especially since I had three mandatory courses and two elective courses.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All my courses were at the undergraduate level. I remember having courses with both second-year and third-year students.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In four out of five courses, the class was very small, around 20-30 students. This created a much closer relationship with the professor, which was very rewarding. Overall, the teaching style was more authoritative and hierarchical compared to Copenhagen. In most of my courses, there was a more empirical focus than in Copenhagen, where we are taught more theory. Generally, the teaching was more broad-strokes rather than delving into the details, if I can put it that way. There was significantly less required reading than in Copenhagen. Instead, there were many oral presentations and written assignments throughout the semester, which is quite intense and requires good planning and time management. Attendance was also mandatory.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: 1) Comparative Politics, 2) Decision-Making Process of the European Union: an Insider's View, 3) European Integration and its Challenges: the Euro, Migration and Populism, 4) Political Identities in the Age of Discontent and 5) Democratic Theory and Democracy in Crisis.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you have an interest in political theory, then choose Political Identities in the Age of Discontent and Democratic Theory and Democracy in Crisis. The professor is an amazing teacher, and you read some very interesting texts.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I lived in a dormitory where cooking facilities were very limited, so I ended up spending quite a bit of unforeseen money on takeaway.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The supermarkets were more expensive than I thought. Bars and restaurants were significantly cheaper than I had expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I do not know. I did not seek them out.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I do not know. I did not have the energy to explore the options because the academic workload was so demanding.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I do not know as I did not participate in it.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I spent a lot of my free time just wandering around the city and getting to know the different neighborhoods. I recommend, of course, visiting the well-known museums, parks, and other attractions. And, of course, enjoying all the delicious French food!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was relatively smooth. It is a big advantage to speak a bit of French. Many people outside the university speak very little English.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I myself did not manage to do that. The French students I was studying with were a couple of years younger and kept to themselves most of the time. However, I made friends among the other exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language barrier.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The French really know how to make the most of the day. Even if you finish work or studies late in the evening, they still go out and enjoy each other's company. French people use the city and public spaces more and often sit alone, sipping coffee and reading a book. There is an atmosphere of enjoying life that you do not find in Copenhagen. They are also more passionate and assertive compared to Copenhageners, which can be very refreshing.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) Determine if you are truly willing to be challenged with a heavy workload. 2) Put effort into finding a place you actually want to live. 3) Practice your French before you go.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember to experience and enjoy the city, even though the university is demanding.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To be academically challenged without losing courage. To create a daily life I enjoyed in a foreign city without my family and friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The weeks when the workload was exceptionally high. The periods when I missed my life in Copenhagen.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: One learns a lot about oneself by going on exchange, both academically and personally.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
